items.title: OpenAI begins rolling out GPT-6 Astra, its first model to cross the 'Critical' cyber threshold
items.summary: On September 3, OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 Astra to a limited set of organizations, with broader access to ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise, the API, and AWS coming over the following days. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, coding, and professional/science tasks, and is also the first OpenAI model to cross the "Critical" tier of its Preparedness Framework for cybersecurity, having independently found and exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in testing — so its most powerful capabilities are gated behind the invite-only Daybreak program.
items.whyItMatters: A jump in general reasoning/coding capability from a frontier lab is worth tracking as a candidate backbone for any agent orchestration Romain/Anna might need beyond pure voice (lesson planning, content generation), and the new safety-gating precedent shows how access to a lab's most capable model can now come with real restrictions.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash and a gated Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber variant
items.summary: Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash on September 2 at the same introductory price as 3.7 Flash ($0.75/$3.75 per million input/output tokens through year-end, cached input at $0.075/M), with gains in agentic software-engineering and multi-step reasoning tasks. Alongside it, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber — a security-focused variant with loosened mitigations for vulnerability discovery — is gated to trusted defenders via Google's new Fairwind Program.
items.whyItMatters: Flash-tier pricing and reasoning upgrades matter for any lightweight backend task around a voice tutor (grading, content generation, lesson-plan drafting) that doesn't need a full frontier model — cheap, capable Flash models are the ones actually worth wiring into a cost-sensitive product.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3, an agent that asks clarifying questions and confirms before acting
items.summary: Meta shipped Muse Spark 1.3 on September 2 with better long-horizon collaboration on coding/agentic tasks — it uses roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than 1.2, generates its own context from messy sources, asks clarifying questions when a prompt is ambiguous, and confirms before taking consequential actions. Pricing is unchanged from 1.2.
items.whyItMatters: The "ask before assuming, confirm before acting" pattern is directly applicable UX inspiration for a tutoring agent — Romain or Anna checking in on ambiguous student intent, rather than guessing, mirrors good pedagogy as much as good agent design.
